what: R survey fixtures for stratified estimation and Neyman allocation
ordering_note: R2.2: every estimator in D2.3 is written against these numbers, which existed first. A test cannot agree with an implementation for the same wrong reason when the expected value predates the implementation.
call_provenance: This exact call was validated against Barnett Table 2B in D2.1 (r/barnett_table_2b.R). No fixture here uses any other design. A different design is not covered by that anchor.

standards.allocation: S-1.2 Neyman (1934); S-1.3 Cochran 3rd ed.; reproduction anchor S-2.3

open_question.title: Rounded Neyman allocation does not always sum to n
open_question.evidence: rare_event_neyman_5000: raw 3844.9/883.9/270.2 rounds to 3845/884/270, which sums to 4999 against a requested 5000. Barnett's case sums exactly, so D2.1 did not surface this.
open_question.why_it_needs_a_ruling: The estimator cannot decide alone. Handing the remainder to a stratum changes a pre-registered design after the operator wrote it, which is V-1's class. Refusing costs an operator a usable plan over one unit. Reporting the sample at its true size is honest but silently delivers less than was asked.
open_question.status: UNRULED -- no code until the director rules

allocation_fixtures.label: barnett_neyman_4000
allocation_fixtures.note: The D2.1 anchor, carried forward as an allocation fixture. Reproduces Barnett Table 2B exactly.

allocation_fixtures.label: barnett_proportional_4000
allocation_fixtures.note: Same frame, proportional allocation. The contrast that shows what Neyman buys: it moves sample into the high-variance strata.

allocation_fixtures.label: two_stratum_neyman_1000
allocation_fixtures.note: The smallest case worth pinning. Hand-checkable.

allocation_fixtures.label: rare_event_neyman_5000
allocation_fixtures.note: The regime this tool exists for. Every stratum rate below 1%, which is where the interval choice in S-1.1 matters most.

q2_floor_case.note: Neyman allocates fewer than 2 units to stratum 2. Zero within-stratum degrees of freedom, so its variance contribution is undefined. ALLOCATION_TOO_THIN refuses here.

estimation_fixtures.label: barnett_design
estimation_fixtures.note: Barnett's allocation, with the nearest whole number of positives to each rate.

estimation_fixtures.label: two_stratum_balanced
estimation_fixtures.note: Small and hand-checkable. Both strata well inside the interval's comfort zone.

estimation_fixtures.label: rare_event
estimation_fixtures.note: Low prevalence throughout -- the regime the intervals were chosen for.

estimation_fixtures.label: one_stratum_zero_positives
estimation_fixtures.note: A stratum with no positives at all. Its within-stratum variance is zero, so it contributes nothing to the SE -- which is correct and surprising, and is why this is pinned.

estimation_fixtures.label: minimum_viable_stratum
estimation_fixtures.note: Two units in one stratum -- exactly Q2's floor. One unit would leave its variance undefined; two is the smallest that works.
